responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the Renesas RL78 microcontroller family, covering the architecture-specific logic needed to lower GCC’s generic RTL into valid RL78 code and assembly. Its central header and main backend implementation files define the RL78 ABI, register classes, calling convention, frame layout, address spaces, target hooks, per-function state, assembler emission, and option-controlled behavior for CPU and multiply/divide variants. The machine-description files provide the target’s operand predicates and constraints, generic-to-target expanders, and the two-stage instruction vocabulary used by the port: a virtual instruction layer for RL78-specific allocation/devirtualization and a real-instruction layer for final opcode selection, peepholes, and flag behavior. The module also integrates RL78-specific C-family language support for __near/__far address spaces and exposes target options that control hardware assumptions, relaxation, simulator behavior, and related code-generation choices. Overall, this directory is responsible for expressing RL78-specific addressing, near/far memory semantics, prologue/epilogue and interrupt handling, instruction selection, late RTL rewriting, and final emission in a form distinct from other GCC target backends.
